sections.body: While you sleep, your brain stores what you learned that day, your body repairs itself, and you grow.
Sleep experts recommend 9–12 hours a night for ages 6–12, and 8–10 hours for teenagers. Many teens get much less.
Too little sleep can make it harder to focus, remember things and control your mood. It can also affect your health.
Teen body clocks naturally shift later, so feeling awake at night is normal. Good habits help: a regular bedtime, a dark, cool room, and no screens for 30–60 minutes before bed.
Bright screens late at night can make it harder to fall asleep. Notifications keep your brain alert too.
Keep a sleep diary for a week: bedtime, wake time and how you feel. Do you see a pattern?

quiz.q: How much sleep do sleep experts recommend for teenagers?
hints: Ages 6–12 need 9–12 hours. Teens need a bit less, but not much less.
If younger kids need 9–12 hours, would teens need only half that?
quiz.explain: Sleep experts recommend 8–10 hours a night for teenagers.

quiz.q: Which habit helps you fall asleep?
hints: Think about what keeps your brain alert.
Screens and caffeine both keep you awake.
A dark, quiet room helps you sleep. Which choice is similar?
quiz.explain: Putting screens away before bed helps your brain wind down.

options: Your brain stores what you learned while you sleep
Sleeping means you don't need to study
hints: What does the brain do at night?
If you practise piano and then sleep well, you often play better the next day. Why?
quiz.explain: During sleep your brain stores and strengthens what you learned.
